answer: Build a vine of verifiable presence: each account must sustain a regular pulse of small, unpredictable, time-boxed tasks, and a missed beat prunes the branch instead of punishing the whole plant. Admission grows only through a signal of mutual, costly attestation: two accounts that vouch for each other stake a deposit that burns if either is later shown a clone. A vine rooted in one real person cannot clone its pulse cheaply, because every copy needs its own heartbeat, stake, and distinct history of useful work. Public logs trace each branch to its root.
